Overview

Build agents that act, not ones that just answer.

Agents That Act: TrueFoundry × Polaris Hackathon is a one-day hackathon built around TrueForge, TrueFoundry's open-source agent harness. The challenge is to build an AI agent that can reach real systems, run the code it writes safely, and know when to stop and ask.

With a ₹3,00,000 prize pool, AWS and OpenAI credits for shortlisted teams, and mentors from TrueFoundry and Polaris, this is an opportunity to build and showcase an agent that does something real.

THE CHALLENGE

Build an agent for a real-world job that is genuinely worth handing over to AI.

Your agent should:

  • Reach a real system such as a database, repository, cloud account, or ticket queue.
  • Run the code it generates safely inside a sandbox.
  • Stop before irreversible actions and wait for human approval.

You can build for any domain. Suggested ideas include cloud cost cleanup, database migration, release management, support ticket resolution, access review, and infrastructure runbooks.

HACKATHON HIGHLIGHTS

  • Build with TrueForge, an open-source MIT-licensed agent harness.
  • Get access to AWS and OpenAI credits for shortlisted teams.
  • Learn from and interact with TrueFoundry and Polaris mentors.
  • Showcase your working agent to the judging panel.
  • Food, power, and Wi-Fi are provided at the venue.

GET STARTED WITH TRUEFORGE

TrueForge is open source, MIT-licensed, and runs locally with one command:

npx @truefoundry/trueforge

Build agents that reach real systems, run real code, and know when to stop.

Themes

Cloud Cost Janitor

Find idle instances, orphaned volumes, and forgotten load balancers, calculate their monthly cost, and draft a teardown plan. Reaches: Cloud billing and infrastructure APIs Approval required: Deleting a resource

Migration Rehearsal Agent

Restore a database copy in a sandbox, run the schema change, compare the rows, and report the results. Reaches: Your database Approval required: Applying changes to production

Release Captain

Read commits since the last tag, run tests in a sandbox, and write release notes. Reaches: GitHub and a package registry Approval required: Tagging and publishing

Agents That ActRead more

Ticket Resolver

Reproduce a bug in a sandbox, return a patch and draft reply, or provide an honest “could not reproduce” result. Reaches: Linear, Jira, or Zendesk Approval required: Replying to the customer

Agents That ActRead more

Access Reviewer

Find permissions that have been unused for 90 days and propose a least-privilege change with its blast radius. Reaches: Your identity provider Approval required: Revoking access

Runbook Executor

Execute a human-written runbook step by step, handling reversible steps automatically. Reaches: Your infrastructure Approval required: Every destructive step

Eligibility

  • Open to participants aged 18 and above.
  • Participants should be able to write code.
  • Participants must be able to attend the hackathon in person in Bengaluru on 26 September 2026.
  • Open to students, working engineers, and founders.
  • No prior TrueFoundry experience is required.
  • Participants can register individually and form teams of 1 to 4 members.
  • Solo participation is welcome.

Rules

1. Eligibility

  • The hackathon is open to anyone aged 18+ who can attend the in-person event in Bengaluru.
  • Participants must be able to write code.
  • Round 1 registration is individual.
  • Teams can have 1 to 4 members, and solo participation is allowed.
  • No prior TrueFoundry experience is required.

2. Building Requirements

  • Projects must be built during the hackathon. Pre-built projects are not eligible.
  • The agent must run on TrueForge.
  • Participants can use any language, framework, or model provider.
  • Prior research and reading the TrueForge documentation are allowed.

3. AI Tools

  • AI assistants such as Claude, Copilot, and Cursor are allowed.
  • Participants must disclose the AI assistants used in their project README.
  • Teams must be able to explain their own architecture and code.

4. Project Requirements

  • The agent must reach a real system or tool.
  • Generated code must run safely inside a sandbox.
  • The agent must stop and request human approval before irreversible actions.

5. Credentials and Data

  • Participants may only connect their own accounts, data, and credentials.
  • API keys and other sensitive credentials must not be included in the repository or demo video.

6. Code of Conduct

  • Participants must maintain a respectful and professional environment with other participants, mentors, organizers, and the venue.
  • Harassment or inappropriate behaviour will not be tolerated.

7. Intellectual Property

  • Participants retain full intellectual property rights to what they build.
  • The organizers may request permission to showcase submitted projects.

8. General

  • The hackathon is free to enter and attend.
  • Participants must follow the instructions provided by the organizers throughout the event.
